newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe Energy Ecuador oil well at 500 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe Energy Ecuador oil well at 500 bpd.

text.p: Santa Fe Energy Resources Inc said Tuesday a new well it was developing in Ecuador was producing at an average rate of about 500 barrels of 30-degree API gravity oil per day.
The company also said it had plugged and abandoned a second well that it did not find to be commercially viable.
Both exploratory wells are located on Block 11, an area of about 494,000 acres in Ecuador's northeastern Oriente Basin, it added.
The first well, known as Cristal-1 on the company's Diamante Prospect, was between 9,764 feet and 9,784 feet deep in the Hollin formation, it said.
"Additional work will be required to more fully define the size of hydrocarbon accumulations associated with the Cristal well," it said.
The second one, called Betano-1, was located on Zafiro Prospect, the company said.

"The ultimate commerciality of Block 11 will depend on the results of drilling on our Rubi (Prospect) located south of the Aguarico River," it said. "We plan to spud the first Rubi wildcat well in mid-1997."
The company said it and its partners had identified some 15 other prospects on Block 11, apart from Diamante and Zafiro.
Petrolera Santa Fe (Ecuador) Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Santa Fe Energy Resources, is operator of Block 11 and holds a 35-percent working interest in it.
Other partners in the consortium Nippon Oil Co Ltd of Tokyo, Yukong Ltd of Seoul and Korea Petroleum Development Corp.
